To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a data acquisition system for a PET scanner based on long axials oriented scintillation crystal, readout by HPDs.

(a) the DAQ system here described is suitable for the read-out of the novel PET scanner based on long axial crystals readout by hybrid photo-detectors (HPD); (b) it has been designed according to the IDEAS VaTA GP5 chip specifications; (c) the system has been developed to study and to optimize the essential design parameter and it is suitable to be used as a stand-alone system for the read-out up to 16 IDEAS VaTA chip per channels
we have developed a data acquisition system for a novel positon emission tomography scanner that is based on long axials scintillation crystals and readout by hybrid photodetectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new PET design based on a new detector and on the development of an event driven DAQ system.
the development of a new type of PET scanner that is able to overcome the limitations of the conventional PET scanner and to achieve high spatial resolution and sensitivity.

the development of a new PET technology, based on the use of a large array of scintillation crystals and of a fast, high efficiency and high spatial resolution readout system, and with the development of the related DAQ system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the system here described has been designed to be flexible and modular, to allow easy and rapid upgrades, to be scalable, to be able to accommodate different readout chips, to be able use the same readout card for different applications, and to be easily interfaced to different computers.
the system is very flexible and can be used in many different ways.
the DAQ is a reliable system, that allows to acquire data with a dead time as low as 0.5%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system has been designed to be flexible, scalable and modular and to allow the use of the most recent readout technologies.
the DAQ system, with a total cost of about 100,000 Euro, is a flexible, low cost and high performance system that can be easily scaled to a 16 module PET system.
the DAQ system is fully functional and ready to be used with the PET scanner prototype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high throughput DAQ can be achieved with a relatively simple system architecture, based on a few, independent and event-driven readout chains.
the system is able to operate in the 100-300 keV range, and is capable of acquiring data from 16 HPDs at the rate of 100 kcps per HPD.
the proposed DAQ system is a very flexible and scalable system that can be easily adapted to a PET scanner with a large number of modules.
